lines: Non-members are always welcome on our trips - please contact the New Members Rep to get put in touch with the trip leader.
Unless otherwise stated, socials are at 110 Waltham Road, Christchurch. Doors open at 7:00 pm with the meeting starting around 7:20 pm and the talk staring at 7:30 pm
Sun 11 October: The Summit Road Emu Parade
Do you remember doing the Emu Parade at School or in Cubs? If not, an Emu Parade is where everyone lines up and moves across a field picking up Rubbish.

I've decided to indulge my nostalgia for Emu Parades and cleaning up obsession by picking up Rubbish on the Summit Road, and since the CTC are quite often using the Summit Road for trips (many of you will have a love-hate relationship due to the Diamond Harbour to Lyttelton walk), it's a good opportunity to show an appreciation for it by making it a little tidier.
The Plan is to spend a few hours picking up Rubbish, the Summit Road Society have indicated a section of the road that needs a bit of Aroha.
2. A stick or walking pole (or something like that) to help pick up stuff
1. Rubbish Bags and a trailer to take rubbish to a transfer station.
2. Hand Sanitiser/ Soap and other stuff to make you feel clean during/ after
So come on, let's show some love of the Summit Road and tidy up a small bit of it!
Mount Garfield is a scenic peak located in the Doubtful Range of the Lewis Pass region in New Zealand's South Island.
• Elevation: ~1,500 m to 1,676 m (depending on the exact high point or ridge points)
• Range: Doubtful Range, Lewis Pass Scenic Reserve area
• Exposure & Terrain: Generally low exposure compared to high alpine climbs, featuring mature beech forest, hidden or marked bush tracks, tussock terrain, and alpine tarns.
• Duration: Usually a full day trip (8 to 9 hours).
We may end up returning the same way
Wed 14 October: Wednesday Social Walk #110 – Heathcote Quarry
Starting from the steps by 160 Bridle Path Road 18:30 / 6:30 PM

We’ll start at the entrance to the Heathcote Quarry reserve, next to the driveway of 160 Bridle Path Road. The upper track through the reserve joins on to the Kenton Track running through Scotts Valley and John Britten Reserves. We’ll go off track for a bit to reach the John Britten Spur track and then the Summit Road. The descent will be down the unofficial Morgan’s Track and back to the lower track through the Heathcote Quarry Reserve. Parts of Morgan’s Track are a bit steep and scrambly, but slow and steady will get you down just fine.
The total distance is 7.8 km with about 430 metres elevation gain, expect to take about 2 – 2.25 hours.
It will be dark by the time we finish (sunset at 19:51) – Bring a Headlamp!!!.
Note that you can claim one Wednesday Social Walk towards the three qualifying trips for club membership.
Fri 16 October: French Ridge Hut and Mt French
Day 1. Leave 12.30pm. Drive to Wanaka and Raspberry Flat car park. Arriving at 6.30pm. Walk into Aspiring Hut, arriving about 9pm.
Day 2. Tramp up the valley and up to French Ridge Hut. About 6 hours with 1000m ascent.

Day 3. Up early (5am) to catch the freeze and the sunrise to climb up to The Quarterdeck and abit further to Mt French, 800m ascent. Return to French Ridge Hut for lunch and back to Aspiring Hut for the night.
Day 4. Walk back to the car park and drive home before rush hour traffic.

I've been to Mt French twice before. From either The Quarterdeck or Mt French you will have the closest view and one of the best views of Tititea you will get without actually climbing the mountain. Ice axe and crampons are necessary to access the Quarterdeck.
People are welcome to come if they only want to come to French Ridge Hut only.

Aspring Hut and French Ridge Hut will need to be booked before hand. Aspring Hut bookings should not be a problem, but French Ridge Hut has limited beds and can be popular, so we will need to watch both the forecast and the hut bookings.
You will need to take afternoon of Friday 16 October off work (or maybe the whole day) and Monday 19 October off work.
Trip is very weather dependent and will only leave on a good weather forecast. Good chance that the trip dates will need to postponed.
The trip may be cancelled at short notice or may go at short notice. So participants need to be flexible with your time off work and availability.
Sat 17 October: Goat Hill Plus Plus
We'll go up to Goat Hill, then continue along the ridge for a bit until turnaround time.
Goat Hill return is 10km, 1200m elevation gain.

This is a well appointed hut in behind Mt Thomas with a nice track, making an easier end of easy/.moderate tramp. There is a crossing of the Okuku River at the start; so you can wear old shoes or sandals for this, changing into boots for the walk which is mainly in beech forest. Look forward to lunch at the hut before returning the same way. Return trip 5 hours, 12kms.
Sat 17 October: Mt Clara and something shorter
Ice Axe, Crampons, Helmet, Snow Skills

Plan A: Leave Saturday afternoon and drive Hanmer, probably climb Mt Isobel but maybe Maukuratawhai. We will then head to the former Fowler Hut site (or potentially Lake Tennyson if what somewhere a bit classer) and set up camp for the night.

Sunday morning we will start bright and early following the track to Fowler Pass before turning off heading up to Mt Pickett and then on to Mt Clara. On the return trip we have the option to return the same way or descend the spur from Mt Catley back to the car park.
If time allows I may be persuaded to stop at the hot pools. We will stop a t Brew Moon for dinner in the way home.
I suspect snow gear will be required to summit but I am open to people without snow skills signing up in the understanding you may have to turn around before the summit.
I may slide this trip forward to a Friday night departure if the weather looks better on Saturday than Sunday.
For more info on Mt. Clara https://hikingscenery.com/mt-clara-fowlers-pass-st-james-conservation-area/

A beginner's guide to getting lost and what to do about it, plus some general navigation and bushcraft skills. This is a day of practical training to help prepare you for the day when your planned day walk becomes a potential overnight sleepover. Bring your normal day pack and gear, a good lunch and a sense of humor – some older pre-torn clothes may be useful as the trip does involve some bush bashing. Bring your GPS and/or compass if you have one, but it is not essential because they will be provided for the navigation part of the exercise. We will stop at the Winne Bagoes for tea, a Q&A session and a trip debrief on the way home, because the trip lasts till until 5 - 6pm depending on your navigation skills. This is the only club training course which is open to non-members, and it is designed for trampers looking to step up from easy to moderate trips.
Sun 18 October: Hills of the Waimakariri Basin series No 5: Sugar Loaf by the Settlement of Cass
West Melton Community and Recreation Centre 7.30 am
Come join the fifth tramp in the Hills of the Waimakariri Basin series. A hill the CTC haven't visited in at least a decade ...

Sugar Loaf at 1410 m is located on private land next to the small settlement of Cass. The mountain overlooks the Waimakiriri river and will provide good views of previous hills summitted in the series and other hills in the series to come.
We will ascend a steep ridge to the summit, hopefully avoiding the matagouri and return the same way.

Please note: As the leader likes a long lunch, lunch will be at least half an hour. It is an expectation that the group will regroup frequently at key points. If you are of a fast pace and are unprepared to wait please consider another tramp. As a guide you must be capable of ascending Foggy Peak comfortably within 2 and a half hours.
Total elevation gain approx. 850 metres, the trip will be entirely off track.
Please note the departure point and time.
*** When signing up please comment if you have a current first aid certificate or medical experience. Priority sign up will be given if you do. ***
The leader is happy for people to meet at Z Russley if someone is prepared to arrange this. Please comment in trip sign up.

Wed 21 October: Mark's Cookery Competition- MasterChef version 2.0Social
Since last years MasterChef Cooking competition was such as success, let's do it again!
I'm going to change it up a little this year, there are going to be three categories:
1. Vegetarian/ Vegan - since we have quite a few Vegetarians/ Vegans in the club, create a vegetable based culinary extravaganza
2. A Sweet treat- who doesn't like a treat after a hard day!? create a special something to excite the taste buds
3. Pimped up Dehy- have a special ingredient (or ingredients) that turns Dehy into Delicious? wow us
The rules (pretty much the same as last year):
- Maximum weight of ingredients (excluding Cooker, utensils etc) = 500gms (I have a scale this year!)
- You can do pre-prep of ingredients
- You can't use the Meeting room kitchen except to get water
- Non-perishable food only (so no raw meat or fresh Milk)
- 25 minutes to cook and present, then 10 minutes for the rest of us to taste
- It can be entree/ main or dessert
- For the Dehy, can be any pre-packaged meal.
- Have the recipe and ingredients handy, as we may want to try out making ourselves (like last year, I'll put them on the CTC FB page afterwards).
A winner for each category will be decided by all in a popular vote, and like last year, there will be prizes, maybe some trophies.
Not prepared to be a MasterChef but fancy yourself as a master food critic? come along and taste some yummy food then vote on the best.
Fri 23 October: Hurricane hut labor weekendFull
Drive to brew moon have dinner
(Might stay in murchison rather than lake matiri hut)
Have a swim at secret swimming spot 20min
We will be dropping down from point 1326 to the clearing 736 then joining the track. There is some bush bashing and some bluffs so navigate
Sunday is all off track the ridge line looks pretty good but there will be bush bashing. Monday is pretty overgrown and muddy be prepaid for some type 2 fun. .
Fri 23 October: Extended Labour Weekend:  Greenstone Caples (girls trip)
Z Rolleston (note not one of the usual departure points) 6:30am sharp (this means driving off at 6:30am, so please arrive by 6:15am to load up)
Please note that this is one of the occasional girls-only trips offered within the wider club programme.
Rain or shine, this is going to be a gorgeous trip.
We'll do the circuit as Caples first, then Greenstone.

Tramping will be in the river valleys, mostly flat, and quite an easy track. Great views of the mountains everywhere, some lovely rivers, and patches of forest to keep it interesting. I will also be looking for swimming opportunities, so there will likely be breaks at good swimming places too.
This is an extended Labour weekend trip, so you'll need to have Friday 23rd off work as well as the public holiday.

Fri 23/Oct - Early start drive to the Greenstone carpark near Glenorchy. We'll walk into Mid Caples hut for the night. We may be arriving at the hut after dark depending on driving conditions and walking speeds. Approx 9km tramping, 3 hours. Est 8 hour drive with stops.
Sat 24/Oct - Further up the Caples valley and over McKellar Saddle to McKellar hut. McKellar Saddle and Lake McKellar en route. Approx 22km, 8 hours.
Sun 25/Oct - Down the Greenstone valley to Greenstone hut. Approx 18km, 7 hours.
Mon 26/Oct - Early start out to the road end, and drive back to Christchurch. Approx 12km tramping, 4 hours. Est 8 hour drive home with stops.

All huts and campsites on this track need to be booked online in advance. Once your trip registration is confirmed, you are responsible for booking your own hut/camping spaces and confirming to the trip leader. As it's a public holiday weekend and a popular track, it's likely to get booked out, so get in early.
This trip will be at a relatively slow/relaxed pace. Please only sign up if you are prepared to stay with the group.

Please note: This is one of the occasional girls-only trips offered within the wider trip programme. These trips provide an opportunity for female club members to tramp together in a relaxed and supportive environment. Registrations for this trip are therefore limited to girls only. Thank you for your understanding.
Sat 24 October: Labour Weekend: Tablelands CircuitFull
Now that access to the Flora Carpark in the Kahurangi has been restored its time for an adventure to the Tablelands.

Day 1: Drive to Flora carpark and tramp to either Salisbury Lodge or Balloon Hut (both are bookable huts), or may decide to camp I'll firm up the plan in the next week. Passing the so cool huts huts along the way (some are built into the rock face). Day1 will be a hut baggers paradise with about 5 huts to visit along the way. Approx 6hr drive plus 6hrs tramping (it is an easy track).

Day 2: We will follow the track to Lake Peel and then climb Mt Peel and circumnavigate the lake before carrying on to join the Bullock Track (optional side trip to visit Myttons hut). Depending on time/energy levels we could then climb Gordons Pyramid via the Cloustons Mine Track. I haven't decided where we will spend the second night maybe Gridiron hut, maybe Flora, maybe somewhere randomly in between. Probably about 20km depending on side trips.
Day 3: Walk out via the Lodestone track and then drive home, should be back at a fairly respectable time.
Whilst the road to Flora has been repaired the research I have done suggests a 4wd/awd vehicle is required.

If we can't get suitable vehicles or the more likely scenario that the weather isn't playing ball we will resort to plan B in totally the opposite direction, likely visiting Otamatapaio Hut in the Mackenzie country but TBC.
Sat 24 October: Mt Pfeifer Biv and tarns. Labour Weekend.Full

Mt Pfeifer Biv is located on the Aicken Range, more or less directly above Lake Kaurapataka. We start at the Deception River via Paratu Creek and Waharoa Saddle. It looks like a very steep climb. One of which I have not done before. The biv only sleep 2, so everyone will need to bring tents. The middle day will be to explore and relax.
Sun 25 October: Mt Oxford Loop & Waterfall
🏔️ Mt Oxford Summit & Ryde Falls Loop 💦

Break up that long weekend with an epic day in the foothills! for stunning panoramic views across the Canterbury Plains, then looping back via the Korimako Track and Ryde Falls, with a high chance of a refreshing dip to cool off those legs!
7:20 AM – Meet Up: Gather at Z Papanui (Map Link: https://maps.app.goo.gl/2d1bmmvJHxnKvB7t6) for 7:30 AM – Departure
*Pit Stop: Quick bathroom break in Oxford township (Map Link: https://maps.app.goo.gl/zZPjKWdMzNKxtb566)
8:30 AM – All Arrive at Coopers Creek Carpark & boot up! (Map Link: https://maps.app.goo.gl/7eUZkLhT4xYWmqhn8)
~12:00 PM – Summit & Lunch: Top of Mt Oxford (1,364m) Enjoy 360° views with your sandwich.
Post-Hike: On the drive home, stop off at Oxford Workingmen's Club for a cold drink a warm chat! (Map Link: https://maps.app.goo.gl/yCwxBQQVhAEaozzj6)
Pack your togs & towel: There are two possible swimming spots—Ryde Falls & Coper Creek (end of the track)!
Bring 2-3 litres of water, snacks, layers for the summit (it can go super windy!), and sturdy hiking boots for very likely muddy tracks and snow (no crampon needed)
Mon 26 October: Lyttelton circumnavigation - Labour Day
$0 for members, $5 for non-members + whatever you want to spend on snacks
Corner Norwich Quay / Oxford St, Lyttelton. Near to bakery and pie shop if you need to stock up befo Bus due in just after 9am, so will meet around 9:15am, and set off shortly after

Starting in Lyttelton, we'll walk past the marina and on to the track to Cass Bay. It's a relatively flat start, but from Cass Bay we'll take the very steep Steadfast track to the Crater Rim. We'll traverse the Crater Rim past the gondola and towards Tauhinukorokio / Mt Pleasant. Somewhere along there, we'll stop for lunch. Mt Pleasant will be the high point from which we begin to descend back to Lyttelton, gradually at first before getting steeper. Once finished, we can stop in Lyttelton for some refreshments.
There are plenty of historical features to gawp at along this route if that's your thing - mainly old military buildings and structures from war times.
There are also options to return to Lyttelton if you would prefer a shorter trip.
Expected time: ~5-6 hours, including lunch stop somewhere on the tops
Sat 31 October: Te Ara Pataka Summit Walkway Pettigrews Road to Mt Fitzgerald Return

The trip will start at Pettigrews Road, just off the Summit Road above Pigeon Bay, and follow Pettigrews Track before joining Te Ara Pataka. The track passes across farmland before going through the Whatarangi Totara Reseve. We will go briefly off track with a short gentle climb up to Mt Sinclair (841m). Rejoin the track, then a short steep climb around and up to Mt Fitzgerald (826m). Along the way, great views of Pigeon Bay, Port Levy and a 360 degree perspective of Banks Peninsula. Return the same way. Overall height gain 500m, return trip 16kms.

Wed 4 November: Nepal mini series part 1: Where the mountains reach the sky - with Carol ArmstrongSocial

Carol has travelled to Nepal 6 times, during the 1990s and more recently in 2023 and 2026 . From wild water rafting, visiting Chitwan NP to the endless stunningly beautiful trails throughout the Everest Region and Annapurna region. This time our footsteps took us to Gokyo Lakes and over Renjo La Pass @ 5345m Photos and thoughts from our trip to Gokyo Lakes and may be a few from EBC in 2023. Q&A welcome - from choosing a guide / trekking agency, challenges of walking at altitude, fitness, etc ....
Wed 11 November: Wednesday Social Walk #112 – Rogaine(ish) in Vic Park
Sign of the Takahe Toilet block. 18:30 / 6:30 PM

I’ve hidden ten mini-road cones in Victoria Park. Your mission – should you decide to accept it – is to retrieve the cones so I don’t have to go collect them the following day. There will be a map provided which looks like a regular rogaining map. And there will be a clue sheet to help you find the locations.
Where this differs from normal rogaining is that we’ll do it as a group – I don’t want people spread out all over the hills in the dark and waiting for them to return to home base.

We should be able to nail this in about the usual two hours. If we get through it too quickly we can go home early or just walk around in the dark until the 2 hours are up, and if it’s taking too long we’ll just hot-foot it back to the start and I’ll pick up any remaining markers the next day.
Sunset is at 20:28 – Bring a Headlamp just in case.
#### If you’ve done this trip before, you’re welcome to join us for the walk, but please don’t give too many hints to the newbies; just tag along and enjoy watching them getting lost. ####
Note that you can claim one Wednesday Social Walk towards the three qualifying trips for club membership.
Fri 13 November: Canterbury Anniversary Canter- Mt OwenFull
Z Papanui or something like it We'll depart on Thursday after work - 4pm would be ideal
It's been a while so time to go back to Mt Owen in Kahurangi NP and do a little more exploring.

We'll leave on Thursday after work (the earlier the better but I think 4pm would work for most people) and drive up to some Accommodation - where exactly is TBC, I forgot where we stayed last time so will need to look into.

On Friday, we'll drive to Courthouse Flat carpark and start the trudge uphill to Granity Pass Hut which is likely to be busy so I'm thinking we walk a bit further and camp somewhere, either up at the tarns by Sentinel Hill or in the valley just past the hut - can vaguely remember seeing a nice camp spot by an overhang.

On Saturday, we'll go up to Mt Owen, it wasn't too bad last time, just be aware there's some rocks/ boulders/ Gaps and likely some soft snow (not the crampon type but snow). That won't take us the whole day so there is ample opportunity to do some more exploring afterwards - it looked quite explorer friendly.
On Sunday we'll pack up the tents, head down hill and drive home, there will be time for a dip in the river before we leave, don't expect to be home before 8pm.
1. Bring a Tent - the Huts for softies!
2. there is a Ford before Courthouse Flat, it's not monster truck category but your average sedan might be a bit risky.
Courthouse Flat to Granity Pass Hut - 8.3km, roughly 1100m of Elevation Gain, add another 250-300m of gain if we camp by the tarns
Granity Pass Hut to Mt Owen - roughly 3-4km, 700m of elevation gain
Fri 13 November: Show weekend lake Morgan loop

3-day circuit of the Morgan Tops, coming up the Crooked River to Top Crooked then climbing up onto and traversing the range via Lake Morgan Hut, continuing south past O'Shannesy and descending back into the Crooked via a fabulous Permolat track at the southern end of the range.
Will be tenting on the tops by some tarns
Will take tools for track cutting not main focus of the trip but. Good to do some
May do trip in reverse depending on weather
Starting from Sharplin Falls car park, we will climb the South Face Track before turning onto the summit track and making our way to the summit of Te Kiekie (Mount Somers) 1,687 m.
From the summit, we will descend the Te Kiekie Route on the northern side of the mountain. This steep, poled route takes us down to the Mount Somers Track near the saddle.
From there we will continue to Pinnacles Hut, before following the track down Bowyers Stream, over Duke Knob back to Sharplin Falls car park.
The full circuit is approximately 17 km, with about 1,400 m elevation gain.

This is a long day over steep and rugged terrain, with much of the upper route exposed to the weather. Participants should be comfortable with a full day of tramping with sustained climbs and descents.
Please note: The departure point and time.

If weather conditions at Mt Somers are unsuitable but are favourable further north, the alternative trip will be the Coopers Creek- Mt Oxford-Ryde Falls circuit. If neither location has suitable conditions, the trip will be cancelled.
Wed 18 November: Nepal mini series part 2, The Highs and the Lows: Tramping in the Himalayas with Sushil PoudelSocial

Are you curious about how tramping culture is evolving in the small Himalayan country of Nepal? Once enjoyed solely by international visitors, the trekking trails are now seeing a growing number of young local adventurers. Before moving to New Zealand, I used to lead tramping trips in Nepal. Join me for a talk exploring the highs and lows of trekking in the Himalayas, the changing outdoor culture in Nepal, sustainability of mountain tourism and some insights from my personal experiences on the trails.

Wed 2 December: All I want for ChristmasSocial

Final club rooms social evening of the year. Bring along your Christmas plans, your top tramping related gift suggestions or your favourite tramping gadgets to discuss with other club members before we go our separate ways for the summer.
Thu 3 December: Waimak Gorge Kayak / Packrafting Trip 🛶
Mt White Bridge → Waimakariri Gorge Bridge
2 days | Late November – early December | Dates flexible
I’m looking to lead a 2 day kayak/packrafting trip down the Waimakariri River, starting at Mt White Bridge and paddling through the gorge to Waimakariri Gorge Bridge.

The plan is to take our time and stay in either Hamilton hut or Walker hut along the way rather than trying to smash it out in a day (though this might be plan B). I’ll also be using the trip as an opportunity to practise my newly acquired whitewater skills, so where we find suitable rapids I’ll likely be getting out, walking back upstream and having another go!

Experience: Participants MUST have completed Grade 2 kayak training or have equivalent Grade 2 whitewater experience. This isn’t a beginner/instructional trip, so everyone needs to be comfortable looking after themselves on Grade 2 water. FYI, I have only just completed my Topsport Grade II course
Gear: BYO kayak or Packraft, paddle, PFD, helmet, spray deck and other appropriate whitewater and overnight gear.

Dates: Flexible at this stage. I’m aiming for a suitable 2 day weather/river-level window sometime during the last three weeks of November or first week of December. We can settle on dates based on the group, conditions and forecast.
Expect a relaxed adventure, some good river scenery, hut nights and plenty of laughs 🤞
Get in touch if you’re keen!
Z (formerly Caltex) Russley AM and PM departure
Rope-free, helmet-compulsory, headlamps-essential, type-2-fun all the way.
Friday, my car will leave town earlier as I want to take a wander up Otira Valley to contemplate a future rollie-pollie. The other car will depart 4-5pm ish for people who can’t leave town early.
Saturday, alpine start, Goat Hill to Mt O'Malley (including Mt Cassidy & Mt Aicken)
Sunday, subalpine start, recovery day ala Rome Ridge to Mt Bealey
If the weather is moist, we will do wet weather related activities.
There is no gpx route, I don’t know the way, given the trip grade, you are expected to do your own research.
We need 2 cars to make this happen, car shuffle.
Wed 16 December: Christmas Dinner at a restaurantSocial
Thu 17 December: Ice Lake Revenge - New Dates Part 2Full
Moderate/Hard but at a Moderate Pace
Z (formerly Caltex) Russley 6 pm on Thursday, 17 December

Please note that the dates for this trip are subject to change as it is very weather-dependent. If bad weather presents itself, I will not cancel this trip, only reschedule for a later date. We will also consider adding one other car if we manage to garner interest.
Also note: Last year, we never got to Ice Lake because of how high the river was to cross the top branch of the Butler. This year, we are coming back for revenge!
We will leave Christchurch around 6 pm on Thursday with a plan to overnight in Arthur’s Pass at the club hut.

The next morning, we will have an early start (in the car by 4 AM!) with the goal of reaching Whataroa as early as possible to start tramping (should be around 7 AM). About 5ks out of Whataroa, we will find the trailhead. After parking the car, we will head up the valley. Should be a relatively easy 7.5ks to the Perth River Junction (2 hours). From there, the track gets a bit more exciting. According to DOC, this should take around 7 hours to get up to Top Butler Hut (but last year it took us 10).

The aim is to stop at Top Butler Hut for the night! What does this mean for you? Well, epic views and a decent hut and... a full 12 to 13 hours of tramping on day one. I know it sounds crazy, but it is doable!

This year, I will be watching the weather like crazy to find a long dry spell to make sure that we will, in fact, be able to cross the top branch of the Butler! Once we have done so, we will rejoice and then head off up the last 2 hours of track (with our track record - pun intended - it will probably take around 4 hours). Either way, we should have a full day in which we make our attempt to reach Ice Lake. Depending on when we do so, we will try to get a fair bit of the way out before we camp for the night (probably somewhere along the track like we did last year).
We finish whatever we didn't do yesterday and then start the long drive back, victorious, knowing that Ice Lake did not beat us again.
7.3km from the carpark to Perth River Track Junction (2 hours)
9.06km from Perth River Track Junction to Butler Junction Hut (6 hours)
5.81km Butler Junction Hut to Ice Lake (~6 hours. 4 hours to Top Butler Hut and 2 hours (?) to the lake)
Important things to keep in mind:
- Please bring a tent. The huts are not bookable, and we don’t want to be forced to overnight at huts due to one person not bringing a tent.
- These will be very long days (but worthwhile!). Be sure that you are ready for 12+ hours of West Coast tramping with a full pack!

- Our pace is steady, but NOT FAST. Trey has type-1 diabetes and we need to stop regularly to check his blood sugar levels. If you are keen to go with us, please come prepared for moderate tramping with frequent stops. I won't allow our group to split up, so if you are fast, please come with patience.
- For those who are keen (and faster than we are), I will bring some tools to help clear some track while you wait for us to catch up.
Tue 22 December: A Very Mark Christmas - George SoundFull
I liked it so much the first time, I am going to go back, this time for Christmas!
22nd December - drive down from Christchurch and stay (camp?) somewhere close to Te Anau Downs so we can be at the Boat ramp nice and early.
23rd December - catch the boat across Lake Te Anau and up Middle Arm, portage to Lake Hankinson and get dropped off, then it's a 2-3 hour walk to Thompson Hut

24th December - A BIG DAY, walk up and over Henry Pass, then down to Lake Katherine, around Lake Katherine and down to the Hut at George Sound. while it is around 10km distance, it will likely take 10-12 hours as it is slow going!

25th December - Spend a cruisy Christmas Day at George Sound - Eating/ exploring/ Swimming etc (weather permitting of course!), last year I carried a rock melon, maybe this year I'll carry something christmassy!
26th December - time to come back, but this time stopping at Henry Pass to camp and hopefully climb some nearby peaks.
27th December - Walk back to Hankinson Hut

28th December - Spend a chilled day at the Hut before getting picked up by the boat and, depending on pick up time, drive some of the way home (not likely to be very far as Boat pick up is around 5pm).
I am open to continuing the fun with another trip in Fiordland if options arise and people are open (i.e. one car could come back and one car stay down there)
I'd rate this trip as a 9 out of 10 on the "Mark Fun" scale, (Dusky is 10/10), you can get a bit of a taste of what Mark fun is by reading the previous trips report:
or via reading about the Route on the Doc Website:
or by looking at a YouTube video of last time (Aaron Zhou captured the "fun")
We'll confirm pick up point/ time closer to the date, but it won't be early as we have a day to get to Te Anau.
- Boat: Indicative cost is $250 per person (based on 8 of us) for boat to and from track.
- Fuel will be the normal Mark long range Fuel Calculation (Fuel cost + 50%), last time it was around $150 each.
- The Huts are backcountry/ non bookable so Hut pass or tickets
- Bring a tent (for Henry Pass and "Just in case")
Sat 9 January: Love Our Huts - Wharfedale Hut
Z Russley 8am at Z Russley to carpool or 9am at View Hill car park
I've signed up to give Wharfedale Hut a clean and it'd be great to have some CTC buddies join me!

Wharfedale has either 8 or 10 bunks (DoC website says 10 while Love Out Huts says 8 so we will find out when we get there, unless somebody knows for sure...?). We may not be the only ones there, so bring a tent or other shelter in case it's full.
Distance from View Hill Car Park to Wharfedale Hut: ~15km
Further information on DoC or Plan My Walk websites - https://planmywalk.nz/tracks/wharfedale-track
DoC says the walk will take 5 hours, which should allow us enough time to get to the hut in time to give it a clean and have a look around. We'll stop for lunch along the way.

Once we get to the hut, assuming no-one is there, the idea is that we give it a bit of a spruce-up for FMC's wonderful Love Our Huts campaign. We may have to wait until the morning for our clean if it happens to be full. Please bring a cleaning cloth. I can bring everything else. We will have to remove any rubbish we find there as well.
More about Love Our Huts here - https://loveourhuts.org.nz/huts/wharfedale-hut
There is a waterfall and swimming hole nearby, which will be great if it's a hot January weekend.

There are a couple of fords to cross on the road in, so SUVs are preferable if you have one. I have driven my little car there before - it is possible, but definitely more comfortable in an SUV especially if it's been raining.
Sat 20 February: A Goat filled weekend
Saturday: We'll go up to Goat Hill, then continue along the ridge for a bit until turnaround time.
Goat Hill return is 10km, 1200m elevation gain.
Plan at this stage is to stay in the club lodge, but I need to check availability.

Sunday: Starting from the deception bridge. We will make like the coast to coasters and complete goat pass in a day. As it is the weekend after the main event we will run a competition to see who can collect the most rubbish (I'm expecting to fill my pockets with gel corners).

Logistics are obviously a bit of an issue on day 2 so if anyone only wants to do day 1 and have a chill day in AP let me know, otherwise I'll see if any of the other leaders want to run the crossover or a two day goat pass womble in the reverse direction.
Fri 6 August: Hooker Hut, Aoraki Mt Cook.Full
Friday 6 August 2027 at 12.30pm. Drive to Aoraki Mt Cook and walk into Hooker Hut for the night.

Saturday 7 August 2027. Free day to relax by the hut or walk to Lake Hooker or depending on weather and snow conditions a day trip to Sefton Biv, bring your favourite mountaineering book and a ghost story as Hooker Hut is reputed to be haunted.
Sunday 8 August 2027. Walk back to the cars and drive home by approximately 3pm.

Since Hooker Hut was restored several years ago it has now become one of the most popular huts in New Zealand. Hooker Hut is set about 20 mins off and out of sight from the Hooker Valley tourist track. It is a peaceful scenic cozy location at the foot of Mt Sefton with views of Aoraki from the hut. Obtaining a booking for Hooker Hut over weekends is very competitive.
Please Read and Understand the Following:
1. Once the second half of 2027 hut bookings open in May 2027 I will endeavor to book all 8 bunks for two nights. At current hut fee prices it will cost me $800 to book the hut.
2. Trip will be first weekend in August (or second weekend in August).
3. The trip will only go ahead if I am successful in securing the booking.
4. If I am successful in booking the hut I will contact the people who have signed up to pay me their $100 hut fees to confirm their place.

5. * If you sign up for the trip please commit to the trip. If you sign up and pull out and there is no one to replace your spot you will forfeit the hut fees you have paid and will be expected to pay your share of the vehicle running costs.

6. Trip will only go ahead if a total of 8 people sign up for the trip. If less than 8 people sign up 15 days prior to the departure date the trip will be cancelled and those who have signed up will collectively contribute to the 10% to 20% penalty I will have to pay DOC for cancelling.
7. Trip will go ahead regardless of the weather forecast, unless the roads are closed. In which case I will need to talk with DOC to see if we are eligible for a refund.
I have been to Hooker Hut twice now. It is an enjoyable relaxing weekend away in a cozy warm historic hut at the foot of two of New Zealands highest mountains.
The walk from the car park to Hooker Hut will take less than 1 1/2 hours for the whole group. So easy enough to bring most things you like.
If interested you have 12 months to mark this trip into your diary and budget for the trip.

This trip is listed just for people interested in staying in Hooker Hut. But DOC allows for 6 campers to camp outside Hooker Hut. So if a car load of people are interested in camping you can do so, but you will need to book and pay for your camp spot yourself and organize your own transport.
